newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS - CRT sale shows promise of Brazil's telecoms.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - CRT sale shows promise of Brazil's telecoms.

text.p: A Brazilian-Spanish group paid 54.8 percent over base price for a minority stake in a state telecom, delighting markets and showing the promise of Brazil's ambitious privatization program for the sector, analysts said.

The consortium, including Telefonica de Espana SA and RBS Participacoes, bid 681 million reais ($655 million) for 35 percent of Cia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes (CRT) in what is seen as the first opening of Brazil's telecoms to private capital.
"This is a clear sign of interest in Brazilian telecoms," said Jacopo Valentino, analyst for Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in Brazil.
"I didn't think it would be that much over the base price. I imagined something closer to 20 percent," he added.

Analysts, who said the minimum price of 440 million reais ($423 million) set by Rio Grande do Sul state seemed high at nearly $4,000 per line, were stunned by Telefonica's offer of nearly $6,000 a line.
The market average in Brazil is about $2,000 a line.
"This clearly shows that foreign investors are willing to pay a lot more for telecoms than the current prices," said Sergio Missima, an analyst at Brazil's Fator Securities.
"It's good for the sector and it's good for the market. It gave the bolsa new life today," he added.
Indeed, Brazilian telecom stocks surged after the auction, led by a more than six percent rise in Telesp, the Sao Paulo state unit of federal giant Telebras SA.

In 1997, the government intends to break up and begin selling Telebras, including its long-distance unit Embratel and Telesp, and grant concessions for companies to operate services on the B Band cellular frequency.

While Rio Grande do Sul's sale of shares in CRT is not technically a privatization because the state retains 51 percent control, the sale was closely watched as it would set a reference price for upcoming telecom selloffs.

The size of the bids surprised analysts, who likened the RBS-Telefonica bid to Telefonica's purchase in 1994 of control of two Peruvian state telecoms for $2.002 billion, almost quadruple the base price and 2.5 times the nearest bid.

In CRT's case, however, even the losing bid, by a group that included Italy's Stet SpA and Brazilian firm Camargo Correa, was more than most analysts expected. The group offered 667.8 million reais ($642 million).
"In this case, control was not the issue," Valentino said. "I think Telefonica was thinking in terms of a strategic position. They're positioning themselves to bid on Telebras South."
Telefonica already operates telecoms throughout Latin America, including Argentina, Chile and Peru.
